blockingFindings: Reviewer independence is forgeable. scripts/record-holdout-eval.mjs:33-43 and scripts/lib/eval-contract.mjs:302-313 accept any provider string and UUID-shaped sessionId; --session is optional and has no provider-issued verification. A source-only probe produced zero validation errors for a fabricated provider/session, so one model context can masquerade as two holdouts.

Unicode normalization does not close the identity bypass. scripts/lib/eval-contract.mjs:381-397 omits several default-ignorable characters from label normalization, including U+3164. A source-only probe using reviewer-one and reviewer<U+3164>-one with fabricated distinct UUIDs satisfied the complete two-pass/two-holdout stop condition.

The source-limited holdout is not cryptographically bound to the frozen tree it reviewed. scripts/record-holdout-eval.mjs:33-43 validates only provenance.candidateCommit, then lines 57-76 substitute Git-derived tree and governed digest without requiring candidateTree or bundleDigest in the attestation. A reviewer can truthfully inspect one physical bundle while the recorder attaches that judgment to another tree at the named commit boundary.

The browser hard gates overstate their evidence. evals/launch-readiness/evals.json defines logical focus order, keyboard-operable email/LinkedIn/resume actions, and protected/open citation non-rendering, but scripts/run-browser-evals.mjs:227-279 tests only the first Tab stop plus citation link semantics. scripts/lib/launch-evals.mjs:41-72 accepted a source-only synthetic report whose rows contained only route, viewport, and passed=true.

Concurrent intake can misclassify duplicates. scripts/lib/knowledge-tools.mjs:49-90 computes duplicateOf and disposition before acquiring the write lock; lines 93-110 re-read only to alter the ID and never recompute duplicate status or boundary text. Two simultaneous identical new leads can therefore both persist as captured rather than preserving the second as a duplicate.
